title: Finite etale pushforward preserves finite locally constant module sheaves
statement: Let $f:Y\to X$ be a finite etale morphism [def-weil-pbc-finite-etale-category] of schemes [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Let $\Lambda$ be a finite commutative ring and let $F$ be a finite locally constant sheaf of $\Lambda_Y$-modules on the small etale site $Y_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site, def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], i.e. one satisfying the equivalent conditions of [lem-weil-pbc-finite-locally-constant-module-values] (e.g. its condition (1): there are an etale covering $\{V_i\to Y\}$ and finite $\Lambda$-modules $M_i$ with $F|_{V_i}\cong\underline{M_i}$). Then the direct image $f_*F$ [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] is a finite locally constant sheaf of $\Lambda_X$-modules on $X_{\Et}$ in the same sense. This is the module clause of Stacks Project Tag 095B (etale-cohomology, lemma-pushforward-locally-constant), whose 'finite type locally constant sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules' is, $\Lambda$ being finite, the same notion by condition (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-finite-locally-constant-module-values].

proof.text: *Conventions.* Call a sheaf of $\Lambda_T$-modules on $T_{\Et}$ (for a scheme $T$) *FLC* if it satisfies the equivalent conditions (1), (2), (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-finite-locally-constant-module-values]; (1) is the working definition and (2) says: locally constant [def-constructible-locally-constant] and finite (every geometric stalk is a finite set) [def-constructible-finite], i.e. finite locally constant [def-constructible-finite-locally-constant] for the coefficient category of $\Lambda$-modules. For an etale $e:T\to Z$ and a sheaf $G$ of $\Lambda_Z$-modules, $G|_e$ (or $G|_T$) is the restriction $(G|_e)(V\to T)=G(V\to T\xrightarrow{e}Z)$ of that lemma. Two elementary facts. (a) *Isomorphism invariance:* if $G\cong G'$ as sheaves of $\Lambda_Z$-modules and $G$ is FLC with data $\{U_i\to Z\}$, $G|_{U_i}\cong\underline{M_i}$ as in (1), then $G'|_{U_i}\cong G|_{U_i}\cong\underline{M_i}$ (an isomorphism restricts to an isomorphism: its components at the objects $V\to U_i\to Z$), so $G'$ is FLC. (b) *Locality:* let $\{g_a:U_a\to Z\}_a$ be an etale covering and suppose each $G|_{U_a}$ is FLC, with data $\{h_{ab}:U_{ab}\to U_a\}_b$ and finite $M_{ab}$, $(G|_{U_a})|_{U_{ab}}\cong\underline{M_{ab}}$. The composites $g_ah_{ab}$ are etale ([lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation] (2)) and jointly surjective (a point of $Z$ is $g_a(u)$ for some $a$ and $u\in U_a$, and $u=h_{ab}(v)$ for some $b$ and $v$), so they form an etale covering of $Z$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]; and $G|_{U_{ab}}$ (restriction along $g_ah_{ab}$) is literally $(G|_{U_a})|_{U_{ab}}$, both having sections $G(V\to U_{ab}\to U_a\to Z)$ over $V\to U_{ab}$. So $G$ is FLC by (1).

*Restriction along an etale morphism preserves FLC* (Stacks 095A, lemma-pullback-locally-constant, for $e^{-1}$, plus stalks). Let $Z$ be a scheme, $G$ an FLC sheaf of $\Lambda_Z$-modules and $e:T\to Z$ etale. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-locally-constant-module-values] (1)$\Rightarrow$(2), $G$ is locally constant and finite. The inverse image $e^{-1}G$ [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] (the same functor on sheaves of $\Lambda$-modules) is locally constant by [lemma-constructible-pullback-locally-constant] (coefficient category the $\Lambda$-modules), and for a geometric point $\bar t$ of $T$, $(e^{-1}G)_{\bar t}\cong G_{e\circ\bar t}$ by [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-stalk-germ] (applied to the underlying abelian sheaf), a finite set; so $e^{-1}G$ satisfies (2) [def-constructible-finite, def-constructible-finite-locally-constant] and is FLC. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-restriction] (1) there is an isomorphism of abelian sheaves $\rho_G:e^{-1}G\xrightarrow{\sim}G|_T$, natural in the abelian sheaf $G$. It is $\Lambda$-linear: for $\lambda\in\Lambda$ multiplication $m_\lambda$ by $\lambda$ is an endomorphism of the abelian sheaf $G$, $e^{-1}m_\lambda$ is multiplication by $\lambda$ on $e^{-1}G$ (this is how $e^{-1}$ acts on module sheaves) and $m_\lambda|_T$ is multiplication by $\lambda$ on $G|_T$, and naturality of $\rho$ at $m_\lambda$ says $\rho_G\circ e^{-1}m_\lambda=m_\lambda|_T\circ\rho_G$ (the argument of step 2 of [lem-weil-pbc-finite-locally-constant-module-values]). So $G|_T\cong e^{-1}G$ as sheaves of $\Lambda_T$-modules and $G|_T$ is FLC by step 1 (a).

*The construction of $f_*$ commutes with etale localization* (Stacks 095B, proof, first sentence). Let $g:U\to X$ be etale, $Y_U=Y\times_XU$ [def-pc-fibre-product] with projections $f_U:Y_U\to U$ and $g':Y_U\to Y$; $g'$ is the base change of the etale $g$ along $f$, hence etale ([lem-weil-pbc-etale-base-change-finite-limits] (1)). We show $(f_*F)|_U\cong(f_U)_*(F|_{g'})$ as sheaves of $\Lambda_U$-modules. For an object $W\to U$ of $U_{\Et}$: $((f_*F)|_U)(W)=(f_*F)(W\to U\to X)=F(W\times_XY)$ and $((f_U)_*(F|_{g'}))(W)=(F|_{g'})(W\times_UY_U)=F(W\times_UY_U\to Y_U\xrightarrow{g'}Y)$ [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. In the diagram $W\times_UY_U\to Y_U\to Y$ over $W\to U\to X$ both squares are cartesian, so by [lem-weil-pbc-cartesian-square-pasting] $W\times_UY_U$, with its projections to $W$ and (via $g'$) to $Y$, is a fibre product of $W\to X$ and $f$; hence the unique morphism $\kappa_W:W\times_UY_U\to W\times_XY$ compatible with the projections to $W$ and to $Y$ is an isomorphism [def-pc-fibre-product], and as a morphism over $Y$ it is an isomorphism of $Y_{\Et}$. So $F(\kappa_W):F(W\times_XY)\to F(W\times_UY_U)$ is bijective and $\Lambda$-linear (restriction maps of a sheaf of $\Lambda_Y$-modules are linear over the constant $\Lambda$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]). For $h:W'\to W$ in $U_{\Et}$, $\kappa_W\circ(h\times_U\mathrm{id}_{Y_U})=(h\times_X\mathrm{id}_Y)\circ\kappa_{W'}$, both sides being the morphism $W'\times_UY_U\to W\times_XY$ with components $h\circ\mathrm{pr}_{W'}$ and $g'\circ\mathrm{pr}_{Y_U}$ (uniqueness in [def-pc-fibre-product]); so the $F(\kappa_W)$ commute with the restriction maps and form an isomorphism of sheaves of $\Lambda_U$-modules $(f_*F)|_U\xrightarrow{\sim}(f_U)_*(F|_{g'})$.

*A finite etale morphism is etale locally split* (Stacks 095B, proof, second sentence: Etale Morphisms, Lemma 04HN). $f$ is finite and etale [def-weil-pbc-finite-etale-category]. For each $x\in X$, [lem-weil-pbc-finite-etale-etale-local-split] gives an etale $g_x:U_x\to X$, a point $u_x\in U_x$ with $g_x(u_x)=x$, a finite set $J_x$ and a decomposition $Y_{U_x}=Y\times_XU_x=\coprod_{j\in J_x}V_{x,j}$ into pairwise disjoint open and closed subschemes such that each $\mathrm{pr}_2|_{V_{x,j}}:V_{x,j}\to U_x$ is an isomorphism. The family $\{g_x:U_x\to X\}_{x\in X}$ is etale and jointly surjective ($x=g_x(u_x)$), an etale covering of $X$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site].

*The split case: $f_*F$ is FLC on each $U_x$* (Stacks 095B, proof: 'the lemma says that if $\mathcal F_i$ are (finite) locally constant then $\prod\mathcal F_i$ is too'). Fix $x$ and write $U=U_x$, $J=J_x$, $f_U=\mathrm{pr}_2:Y_U\to U$, $g':Y_U\to Y$ as in step 3. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-direct-image-split-cover-product] to $f_U$ with the decomposition $(V_{x,j})_{j\in J}$ of step 4 and $H=F|_{g'}$: with $s_j:U\to Y_U$ the inverse of $f_U|_{V_{x,j}}$ followed by the inclusion (etale), $(f_U)_*H\cong\prod_{j\in J}H|_{s_j}$ as sheaves of $\Lambda_U$-modules. Here $H|_{s_j}$ is literally $F|_{g'\circ s_j}$ (sections $F(V\to U\xrightarrow{s_j}Y_U\xrightarrow{g'}Y)$), and $g'\circ s_j:U\to Y$ is etale ([lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation] (2); $g'$ is etale by step 3), so each $H|_{s_j}$ is FLC by step 2 applied to $Z=Y$, $G=F$, $e=g's_j$. If $J\neq\varnothing$: the finite product $\prod_jH|_{s_j}$ in the additive category of sheaves of $\Lambda_U$-modules is their finite direct sum (biproduct), which is finite locally constant by [lemma-constructible-flc-biproduct] (coefficient category the $\Lambda$-modules, condition (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-finite-locally-constant-module-values]), hence FLC. If $J=\varnothing$: the product is the zero sheaf $0$, which is FLC with the covering $\{\mathrm{id}_U\}$ and $M=0$, the zero presheaf being a sheaf and so its own sheafification, the constant sheaf $\underline0$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. By step 3, $(f_*F)|_{U_x}\cong(f_U)_*(F|_{g'})=(f_U)_*H\cong\prod_jH|_{s_j}$, so $(f_*F)|_{U_x}$ is FLC by step 1 (a).

*Conclusion.* $f_*F$ is a sheaf of $\Lambda_X$-modules [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. The family $\{g_x:U_x\to X\}_{x\in X}$ is an etale covering (step 4) and each $(f_*F)|_{U_x}$ is FLC (step 5), so $f_*F$ is FLC by step 1 (b), i.e. finite locally constant in the sense of [lem-weil-pbc-finite-locally-constant-module-values].

split_report.summary: Statement kept up to the tag: the Stacks tag of lemma-pushforward-locally-constant is 095B, not 03RU (03RU is definition-finite-locally-constant); corrected and the reading of 'finite type' through condition (3) of the module-values lemma added. Proof written along the Stacks proof of 095B in six steps: (1) iso-invariance and etale locality of FLC (elementary, composite coverings); (2) restriction along an etale morphism preserves FLC, via the closed node lemma-constructible-pullback-locally-constant (Stacks 095A), the stalk of an inverse image and the etale identification e^{-1}G = G|_T made Lambda-linear by naturality; (3) f_* commutes with etale localization (explicit kappa_W by pasting of cartesian squares); (4) finite etale is etale-locally split (existing node, Stacks 04HN); (5) split case: one new node lem-weil-pbc-direct-image-split-cover-product (f_* along a split cover is the product of the restrictions to the sheets), then the closed node lemma-constructible-flc-biproduct, empty J handled separately; (6) conclusion by locality. Cycle-creating lemma-weil-pbc-constructible-finite-pushforward not cited.
